articles.title: Zoox's Steering-Wheel-Free Robotaxis Get Green Light to Charge Passengers—a First in the U.S.
articles.summary: Zoox just scored a historic approval: its pod-like robotaxis, which lack steering wheels and pedals, can now collect fares. The Amazon-owned company will start paid rides in Las Vegas, marking a milestone for purpose-built autonomous vehicles.

articles.title: Thumbnail-Sized Bird Figurines Carved 40,000 Years Ago Unearthed in German Cave
articles.summary: Two miniature bird carvings, no bigger than a thumbnail and crafted from mammoth ivory, have been discovered in Germany's Hohle Fels cave. The 40,000-year-old figurines reveal the astonishing artistry of Ice Age humans.

articles.title: MIT Scientists Uncover Why Molybdenum Makes Nitrogen-Fixing Enzymes So Efficient
articles.summary: Two new MIT studies reveal that molybdenum, though it doesn't directly bind nitrogen, helps nearby iron atoms grip nitrogen gas more tightly. This electronic teamwork explains why molybdenum-containing nitrogenases are nature's best ammonia factories.
